findings.title: createrawtransaction rejects an empty inputs array that Core accepts
findings.core_does: AddInputs treats a null or empty inputs array as zero inputs and loops zero times; ConstructTransaction imposes no minimum. createrawtransaction([], {...}) is the standard way to build a funding template and appears at 37 call sites across Core's functional tests, including the three amount-error assertions in rpc_rawtransaction.py:296-299.
findings.we_do: The handler opens with (unless (and (listp inputs) (> (length inputs) 0)) (error ... :message "Invalid inputs")), so an empty array is a hard -8. Executed: dispatch-rpc-method "createrawtransaction" #(#() {"data":"foo"}) => (-8 "Invalid inputs"). The check also masks every later argument error, so the outputs argument is never parsed at all.
findings.impact: Any client that builds an unsigned template with no inputs (the fundrawtransaction / walletcreatefundedpsbt workflow, and Core's own test corpus) gets a hard error instead of a transaction. It also hides all the outputs-argument diagnostics behind a single wrong message.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval: dispatch-rpc-method on a test node with params #(#() <hash-table data=foo>) and #(#() {}) - both returned (-8 "Invalid inputs").

findings.title: createrawtransaction ignores replaceable and version and defaults sequence to SEQUENCE_FINAL, making nLockTime inert
findings.core_does: AddInputs computes nSequence as MAX_BIP125_RBF_SEQUENCE (0xfffffffd) whenever rbf.value_or(true) - and createrawtransaction leaves rbf as nullopt when the argument is absent, so the DEFAULT is 0xfffffffd. Only replaceable=false falls through to SEQUENCE_FINAL-1 (when nLockTime is set) or SEQUENCE_FINAL. ConstructTransaction also takes a version argument (default 2) and rejects anything outside TX_MIN_STANDARD_VERSION..TX_MAX_STANDARD_VERSION (1..3).
findings.we_do: The define-rpc lambda list is ((inputs :array) outputs (locktime :or 0)) - arguments 4 (replaceable) and 5 (version) are declared in our own tables (src/rpc/core-tables.lisp:28,211) but destructured into &rest more and discarded. Sequence defaults to #xffffffff and the transaction version is the literal 2. Executed: with locktime 500 the produced hex ends ...ffffffff01...f4010000 (final sequence, locktime 500); replaceable=false and version=3 produce byte-identical output to the no-argument call.
findings.impact: Three consequences. (1) A transaction built with a locktime is CONSENSUS-FINAL - all-0xffffffff sequences make nLockTime unenforceable - so an operator who asks for a timelocked transaction gets one that can be mined immediately. (2) RBF signalling is inverted relative to Core's default. (3) A client asking for version 3 (TRUC) gets a v2 transaction with silently different relay policy, and an out-of-range version is never rejected.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval: createrawtransaction with one input and one output, varying locktime / replaceable / version. All four calls returned sequence ffffffff and version 02000000.

findings.title: Fee estimator tracks every mempool entry: none of Core's validForFeeEstimation gates nor the txHeight == nBestSeenHeight gate
findings.core_does: processTransaction returns early when txHeight != nBestSeenHeight ("Ignore txs if BlockPolicyEstimator is not in sync with ActiveChain().Tip()"), and then computes validForFeeEstimation = !m_mempool_limit_bypassed && !m_submitted_in_package && m_chainstate_is_current && m_has_no_mempool_parents. A transaction failing any of those is counted in untrackedTxs and never enters the buckets.
findings.we_do: bpe-process-transaction takes only (est txid height feerate) and unconditionally calls NewTx on all three horizons; bpe-note-entry is called from mempool-add-transaction for EVERY successful add, including reorg re-adds, package members and children with in-mempool parents. There is no parameter through which any of Core's four predicates could be expressed, and no height comparison. Executed: a fresh estimator has best-height 0 and still tracks a transaction announced at height 500.
findings.impact: CPFP children teach the estimator that their own (low) feerate confirms in one block, which is exactly the inference the parent paid for. Measured on a synthetic 400-block replay (20 txs/block at 20000 sat/kvB confirming in 3 blocks, plus 20 children at 1000 sat/kvB confirming in 1): estimatesmartfee(2) returned 1000 sat/kvB with children tracked and 20000 sat/kvB with Core's gate applied - a 20x underestimate, in both economical and conservative mode and at both targets tested. The same absence means every transaction replayed from mempool.dat at startup is recorded as if it entered at the current tip (Core drops them all, since nBestSeenHeight is still 0), biasing estimates down after every restart.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval: (a) make-block-policy-estimator + bpe-process-transaction at height 500 with best-height 0 -> tracked count 1; (b) the 400-block differential replay above, run twice, tracking and not tracking the children.

findings.title: decodescript returns the pre-v22 shape and offers p2sh/segwit wrappers Core refuses to print
findings.core_does: decodescript calls ScriptToUniv(include_hex=false, include_address=true), which emits asm, desc, then a single address string and type. It then computes can_wrap, which is FALSE for NULL_DATA, SCRIPTHASH, WITNESS_UNKNOWN, WITNESS_V1_TAPROOT and ANCHOR, and also false for a script that is unspendable, has invalid ops, or contains OP_CHECKSIGADD / an OP_SUCCESS. Only when can_wrap does it emit p2sh, and only when can_wrap_P2WSH does it emit the segwit object - which itself carries asm, hex, type, address, desc and p2sh-segwit. reqSigs and addresses were removed from Core in v22.
findings.we_do: We emit asm and type, then reqSigs/addresses (the removed plural form) for multisig/pubkeyhash/scripthash, a segwit object containing ONLY address, and p2sh UNCONDITIONALLY for every script. desc is never emitted. Executed: decodescript("6a0401020304") returns type nulldata plus p2sh 2NEVj61vjbUGuqGaBVK6YskrXUJyAdb81uM; decodescript of a p2sh script returns another p2sh wrapper; decodescript of a v1 taproot output returns both a p2sh address and a segwit address.
findings.impact: The unconditional p2sh field is the sharp end: we hand out a P2SH address wrapping an OP_RETURN (or wrapping another P2SH, or a taproot output), and anything paid to such an address is unspendable - Core deliberately stopped printing exactly these. The missing desc and the removed reqSigs/addresses break every consumer written against a current Core, and rpc_decodescript.py asserts the modern shape field by field.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval: decodescript on p2pkh, OP_RETURN, p2sh and v1-taproot scripts through dispatch-rpc-method; full result objects captured.

findings.title: decoderawtransaction accepts trailing bytes and has no legacy/witness disambiguation or iswitness argument
findings.core_does: DecodeTx decodes the SAME bytes twice - once with extended (witness) serialization and once with legacy - ignores any serialization that does not fully consume the input (ssData.empty()), and when both succeed picks the one that passes CheckTxScriptsSanity, preferring the extended one on a tie. DecodeHexTx's try_no_witness / try_witness flags are what decoderawtransaction's iswitness argument sets.
findings.we_do: We call bl.ser:read-transaction once on a stream and never check that the stream was consumed; there is no second decode, no CheckTxScriptsSanity tie-break, and the handler's lambda list is (hex-str) - iswitness is not accepted. Executed: decoderawtransaction(<valid tx hex> + "deadbeef") returned :ok, and the echoed "hex" field is the tx WITHOUT the trailing bytes.
findings.impact: A caller is told that a hex string it supplied is a valid transaction with txid X when Core rejects it outright; the txid reported belongs to a truncated prefix of what was sent. A client that round-trips through decoderawtransaction to identify a transaction before broadcasting will identify the wrong one. The missing dual decode also means a hex string that is only valid under legacy serialization is rejected where Core accepts it.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval: dispatch-rpc-method "decoderawtransaction" with a valid 1-in/1-out tx hex plus the four extra bytes deadbeef - returned :ok with the shorter hex echoed back.

findings.title: Script ASM renders small pushes as hex and OP_0/OP_1..16/OP_1NEGATE as opcode names
findings.core_does: ScriptToAsmStr renders a push of 4 bytes or fewer as the DECIMAL CScriptNum value, and GetOpName returns "0" for OP_0, "-1" for OP_1NEGATE and "1".."16" for OP_1..OP_16. With fAttemptSighashDecode (which TxToUniv passes for every scriptSig) a push that passes CheckSignatureEncoding gets its sighash byte stripped and replaced with a "[ALL]"-style suffix.
findings.we_do: disassemble-script emits hex for every push regardless of length, looks every opcode up in *opcode-names* (which yields OP_0, OP_1NEGATE, OP_2 ...), and has no sighash decoding at all - the same function serves scriptPubKey and scriptSig. Executed: 01 64 -> "64" (Core "100"); 02 6400 -> "6400" (Core "100"); 03 20a107 -> "20a107" (Core "500000"); 04 01020304 -> "01020304" (Core "67305985"); OP_0 -> "OP_0" (Core "0"); OP_1NEGATE -> "OP_1NEGATE" (Core "-1"); 52 53 ae -> "OP_2 OP_3 OP_CHECKMULTISIG" (Core "2 3 OP_CHECKMULTISIG").
findings.impact: Every asm field the node emits - decodescript, decoderawtransaction, getrawtransaction verbose, getblock verbosity 2/3, gettxout, scantxoutset, the REST surfaces and the web UI - differs from Core for any script containing a small push or a small-number opcode, which is essentially all of them. A timelock reads as raw hex rather than a block height, and tooling that matches on "0 <20-byte hash>" to recognise a v0 witness program sees "OP_0 ..." instead. rpc_decodescript.py asserts these exact strings at more than a dozen points.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval: bl.val:disassemble-script over eight hand-built byte vectors covering 1/2/3/4-byte pushes, OP_0, OP_1NEGATE, OP_2/OP_3 and a CLTV pattern.

findings.title: estimatesmartfee falls back to a block-percentile estimate where Core reports no estimate
findings.core_does: estimatesmartfee reports estimateSmartFee and NOTHING else. When the policy estimator has no answer it omits the feerate key entirely and returns only {"errors": ["Insufficient data or no feerate found"], "blocks": N}. Core has no secondary estimator, and feature_fee_estimation.py asserts that exact errors array twice - after a backdated fee_estimates.dat and after deleting it.
findings.we_do: estimate-fee-rate asks the policy estimator first and, when it has no answer, falls through to a home-grown percentile of the median feerates of the last N blocks (get-percentile-for-target / fee-rate-percentile), returning it with NO error message - so the RPC reports it as a real feerate. Executed: with an EMPTY policy estimator and 12 blocks of percentile history at median 7 sat/vB, estimatesmartfee(2) returned {"feerate": 7.0e-5, "blocks": 2} where Core returns the errors array.
findings.impact: A wallet or fee UI is handed a number derived from what miners happened to include - the block-percentile heuristic our own estimator's file header explains cannot express 'this feerate FAILED to confirm' - and cannot tell it apart from a real estimate, so it never falls back to its own -fallbackfee. During a lull the percentile sits well below the market rate and the transaction does not confirm. The divergence is deliberate and documented in the source, but it contradicts a contract Core's tests assert.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval: a test node with a fresh make-block-policy-estimator and 12 synthetic block-fee-stats entries; estimatesmartfee(2) and (6) through dispatch-rpc-method.

findings.title: No ParseHashV/ParseHexV: every hash-argument error is ad hoc, and getchaintxstats returns -5 instead of -8
findings.core_does: ParseHashV is one shared helper producing two messages: "<name> must be of length 64 (not <len>, for '<hex>')" and "<name> must be hexadecimal string (not '<hex>')", both RPC_INVALID_PARAMETER (-8). ParseHexV does the same for arbitrary hex. The name is the argument's own name ("blockhash", "txid", "hash", or "parameter 3").
findings.we_do: valid-hex-hash-p is a boolean predicate and each call site invents its own message. Executed, against the exact inputs Core's tests use: getblockheader("nonsense") -> -8 "Invalid block hash" (Core: "hash must be of length 64 (not 8, for 'nonsense')"); getchaintxstats(blockhash="0") -> -5 "Block not found" (Core: -8 "blockhash must be of length 64 (not 1, for '0')") - wrong CODE as well as message; gettxoutproof(["00000000000000000000000000000000"]) -> -8 "Invalid txid 000..."; createrawtransaction([{txid:'foo'}],...) -> -8 "Invalid input txid"; prioritisetransaction('foo') -> -8 "Invalid txid"; getblockfrompeer("1234") -> -8 "blockhash must be a hex string"; getrawtransaction(txid, true, "foobar") -> -8 "Invalid blockhash".
findings.impact: Eight functional-test assertions match these strings verbatim (rpc_blockchain.py:320-321,453-454; rpc_rawtransaction.py:164-167,269-271; rpc_txoutproof.py:60-64; mining_prioritisetransaction.py:218-219; rpc_getblockfrompeer.py:69; wallet_basic.py:172-175). getchaintxstats additionally answers with the wrong error class, so a client cannot distinguish a malformed argument from an unknown block.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval: seven RPCs driven through dispatch-rpc-method with Core's own test inputs.

findings.title: amount-from-value's string path is not ParseFixedPoint: leading zeros accepted, exponents rejected, negative strings mis-coded
findings.core_does: AmountFromValue hands the value's raw string to ParseFixedPoint, which accepts an optional leading '-', a mantissa with NO leading zeros (a lone '0' or 1-9 followed by digits), an optional fraction, and an optional e/E exponent with optional sign; anything else - including trailing garbage - fails with "Invalid amount". Only after a SUCCESSFUL parse does MoneyRange decide between the value and "Amount out of range". Core's own unit tests (rpc_tests.cpp:295-301) pin "1e-8", "0.1e-7", "0.01e-6" and several extreme exponent forms as valid.
findings.we_do: The string branch hand-parses whole and fraction parts with digit-char-p only. Executed: "01" -> 100000000 (Core: "Invalid amount"); "00.1" -> 10000000 (Core: "Invalid amount"); "1e-2", "1e2", "1E8" -> "Invalid amount" (Core: accepted); "-1" and "-0.00000001" -> "Invalid amount" (Core: "Amount out of range", because ParseFixedPoint succeeds and MoneyRange rejects). Numeric JSON amounts take the rational/float branch and do report "Amount out of range" correctly, so only the string spelling diverges. A value at or above 1e10 BTC also reports "Amount out of range" where Core's mantissa overflow gives "Invalid amount".
findings.impact: String amounts are a supported spelling everywhere Core takes an amount, and the wallet tests distinguish the two messages (wallet_basic.py:26,322,433; wallet_bumpfee.py:138,147; wallet_send.py:341,351). A client that sends "-1" as a string is told its amount is malformed rather than out of range, and one that sends "01" gets an amount Core would have refused.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval: bl.rpc::amount-from-value over 19 string spellings.

findings.title: estimaterawfee omits decay and scale and reports feerate 0 where Core omits feerate and reports the fail bucket
findings.core_does: For each horizon that tracks the target Core pushes decay and scale in BOTH branches. On success: feerate, decay, scale, pass, and fail when buckets.fail.start != -1. On failure: decay, scale, fail (the default all -1 bucket) and errors - and NO feerate key, because CFeeRate(0) is the error sentinel.
findings.we_do: The horizon object is built from feerate, pass, fail and errors only; decay and scale are never emitted anywhere in the tree, and on no-answer we emit ("feerate" . 0.0d0) alongside the errors array while omitting the fail bucket. Executed: estimaterawfee(2) on a node with an empty estimator returned {short:{feerate:0.0, errors:[...]}, medium:{...}, long:{...}}.
findings.impact: estimaterawfee is documented as the way to see WHY an estimate came out where it did; decay and scale are two of the five things it exists to report. A client reading feerate cannot tell a real 0 from 'no answer', and check_raw_estimates in feature_fee_estimation.py asserts feerate > 0 for every horizon returned.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval: estimaterawfee(2) and estimaterawfee(2, 0.5) through dispatch-rpc-method on a test node with a fresh estimator.

findings.title: getdeploymentinfo never emits the bip9 signalling string
findings.core_does: Whenever stats are applicable (current state STARTED or LOCKED_IN) Core fills BIP9Info::signalling_blocks and pushes a "signalling" string of '#' and '-' characters, one per block elapsed in the current period, right after the statistics object.
findings.we_do: %bip9-deployment builds bit, start_time, timeout, min_activation_height, status, since, status_next and statistics - and stops. Nothing in src/ computes or emits a signalling string. Executed on a 300-block synthetic regtest chain signalling bit 28: at height 207 the testdummy bip9 object matched Core's expected object field for field except that "signalling" (64 '#' characters) was absent.
findings.impact: rpc_blockchain.py:240 asserts 'signalling': '#'*(height-143) inside an assert_equal of the whole getdeploymentinfo result, so the test fails on the missing key alone. Operators watching an activation lose the per-block view of which blocks signalled.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval: make-versionbits-chain 300 :signal-bit 28, then bl.rpc::%bip9-deployments at heights 207 and 299.

findings.title: getdeploymentinfo reports threshold and possible in LOCKED_IN where Core omits both
findings.core_does: Info() computes the statistics and then, when the current state is LOCKED_IN, OVERWRITES threshold with 0 and possible with false - lock-in is already decided, so there is no threshold left to meet. SoftForkDescPushBack then emits threshold and possible only if (threshold > 0 || possible), so in LOCKED_IN both keys are absent from the statistics object.
findings.we_do: versionbits-statistics returns the deployment's static threshold and a computed possible regardless of state, and the RPC's (when (or (plusp threshold) possible)) guard therefore always passes. Executed at height 299 of a 300-block signalling chain (status locked_in, since 288): statistics came back as period 144, elapsed 12, count 12, threshold 108, possible T - Core would emit period, elapsed and count only.
findings.impact: A client watching an activation sees a threshold and a 'possible' flag for a deployment whose signalling window is over, which reads as though the period could still fail. Field-set divergence in an assert_equal-shaped result.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval: bl.rpc::%bip9-deployments at height 299 of make-versionbits-chain 300 :signal-bit 28.

findings.title: No RPCHelpMan type gate: wrong-typed arguments never produce -3 Wrong type passed, extra arguments are ignored
findings.core_does: RPCHelpMan::HandleRequest first rejects a wrong argument COUNT with the method's help text, then runs RPCArg::MatchesType over every position, collects every mismatch into one object keyed "Position N (name)", and throws a single RPC_TYPE_ERROR (-3) whose message is "Wrong type passed:\n" followed by that object pretty-printed. rpc_blockchain.py:496-506 asserts the entire two-position form verbatim.
findings.we_do: define-rpc only destructures and applies positional coercions; nothing checks a declared type, and dispatch-rpc-method does no arity check. Executed: getblockhash("foo") and getblockhash(true) both -> -8 "Invalid height parameter"; gettxout(txid,"x") -> -8 "Invalid vout"; estimatesmartfee("6") -> -8 "Invalid conf_target, must be between 1 and 1008"; getblockcount(1,2,3) -> succeeds. Grepping the tree finds no occurrence of "Wrong type passed" anywhere. This is DISTINCT from GA10's fixed getnetworkhashps finding (56b53a04): that method now returns -3 with Core's inner sentence, but still without the "Wrong type passed" wrapper and stopping at the first bad position - executed getnetworkhashps("a", []) -> (-3 "JSON value of type string is not of expected type number") where Core reports both positions.
findings.impact: Wrong-typed arguments come back with the wrong error class (-8 instead of -3) and a per-handler message, so a client cannot distinguish 'this is not a number' from 'this number is out of range'; superfluous arguments are silently accepted.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval: eight type-mismatch calls through dispatch-rpc-method plus a scan of *rpc-methods* and a tree grep for the string.

findings.title: createrawtransaction sequence out of range escapes as a Lisp TYPE-ERROR reported as -32603
findings.core_does: AddInputs range-checks the sequence ("Invalid parameter, sequence number is out of range", -8), rejects a missing vout key ("Invalid parameter, missing vout key") and a negative vout ("Invalid parameter, vout cannot be negative"), and ConstructTransaction reports a bad locktime as "Invalid parameter, locktime out of range".
findings.we_do: The sequence is taken straight from the object with no range check and stored into a (unsigned-byte 32) defstruct slot. Executed: sequence 4294967296 raised SB-KERNEL::TYPE-ERROR, which handle-single-request converts to -32603 "Internal error: The value 4294967296 is not of type (UNSIGNED-BYTE 32) when setting slot SEQUENCE of structure BITCOIN-LISP.SERIALIZATION:TX-IN". A missing vout and a negative vout both give -8 "Invalid input vout"; a negative locktime gives -8 "Invalid locktime".
findings.impact: Malformed RPC input surfaces as an internal-error reply carrying an SBCL type-error string and an internal structure name, instead of the documented -8 parameter error. Not a crash - the server catches it - but it leaks implementation detail and gives clients the wrong error class.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval: createrawtransaction with sequence 4294967296, vout -1, vout absent, and locktime -1.

findings.title: Amounts render as JSON doubles instead of Core's ValueFromAmount fixed 8-decimal form
findings.core_does: ValueFromAmount builds a UniValue VNUM whose raw text is strprintf("%s%d.%08d", ...) - always exactly eight decimal places, e.g. 1.00000000, 0.00000000, -0.00001000. UniValue preserves that text verbatim on output.
findings.we_do: satoshi->btc divides by 1e8 into a double-float and yason formats it. Executed through yason:encode: 0 -> "0.0" (Core "0.00000000"); 100000000 -> "1.0" (Core "1.00000000"); 1000 -> "0.00001" (Core "0.00001000"); 21000000 sat -> "0.21" (Core "0.21000000"). Values round-trip numerically (SBCL prints shortest round-trip doubles, so 2099999999999999 renders as 20999999.99999999), so this is presentation only.
findings.impact: Every BTC-valued field in every RPC and REST reply is textually different from Core. Numeric comparisons still succeed, so Core's own assert_equal on Decimal values passes, but any consumer that compares or displays the raw text - and any diff against a Core reply - sees a different document.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval: yason:encode of satoshi->btc over eleven amounts, alongside format-money for the same values.

findings.title: Data must be hexadecimal string omits Core's (not '<value>') suffix
findings.core_does: ParseOutputs parses a data output with ParseHexV(..., "Data"), which on failure throws "Data must be hexadecimal string (not '<the value>')".
findings.we_do: parse-outputs catches the hex-to-bytes error and signals the bare "Data must be hexadecimal string". Executed: bl.rpc::parse-outputs with {"data": "Hello World"} -> (-8 "Data must be hexadecimal string").
findings.impact: wallet_send.py:277 matches on the full string including the suffix, so the substring assertion fails. rpc_rawtransaction.py:296 matches only the prefix and would pass.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval: bl.rpc::parse-outputs on a hash-table {data: "Hello World"}.

findings.title: Verbosity-3 prevout scriptPubKey omits the desc field Core's ScriptToUniv always emits
findings.core_does: TxToUniv renders a verbosity-3 prevout's scriptPubKey with ScriptToUniv(include_hex=true, include_address=true), and include_address is exactly the flag that adds the InferDescriptor "desc" string. The prevout object therefore carries asm, desc, hex, address and type, the same set as a vout.
findings.we_do: input-to-json builds the prevout scriptPubKey by hand as asm, hex, type and optionally address - no desc - while output-to-json (the vout path, same file) does emit desc via scriptpubkey-desc. The two open-coded copies of ScriptToUniv have drifted apart.
findings.impact: getblock verbosity 3, /rest/block/<hash>.json and getrawtransaction with prevouts return prevout scriptPubKey objects missing a field Core documents as always present; a client that reads desc uniformly for vout and prevout breaks on the prevout half.
findings.executed: not executed - read both trees. The vout/prevout asymmetry is visible in the two adjacent functions and in Core's single shared helper.

coverage_note: Covered by execution in the warm container (bitcoin-lisp-dev-50eb89c4558b): rpc/util.cpp's AmountFromValue/ParseFixedPoint (19 string spellings), ParseHashV/ParseHexV messages across seven RPCs using Core's own test inputs, ParseConfirmTarget bounds, the RPCHelpMan type/arity gate, ValueFromAmount rendering, FormatMoney; core_io.cpp's ScriptToAsmStr (eight byte vectors), ScriptToUniv consumers (decodescript on four script classes, tx-to-json/input-to-json/output-to-json read), DecodeHexTx/DecodeTx (trailing-byte and ambiguous-input probes); rawtransaction_util.cpp's ConstructTransaction/AddInputs/AddOutputs/ParseOutputs against createrawtransaction (empty inputs, sequence, vout, locktime, replaceable, version); rpc/fees.cpp's estimatesmartfee and estimaterawfee end to end plus block_policy_estimator internals (constants table checked line by line against block_policy_estimator.h:152-199; TxConfirmStats Record/ClearCurrent/UpdateMovingAverages/removeTx/EstimateMedianVal and estimateCombinedFee/estimateConservativeFee/estimateSmartFee read side by side and found faithful; a 400-block synthetic replay run twice to measure the processTransaction gate); versionbits.cpp Info/statistics and getdeploymentinfo driven across DEFINED/STARTED/LOCKED_IN on a 300-block synthetic chain. NOT COVERED, with the GA11 dimension that inherits each: (1) the fee_estimates.dat wire format - ours is a deliberate own-format v2 file with a CRC32, documented at block-policy-estimator.lisp:637, and no interop with Core's CURRENT_FEES_FILE_VERSION 309900 stream was attempted; the MAX_FILE_AGE / -acceptstalefeeestimates rules were read and match. Inherits: dimension 6 (never-opened files) or a storage reader. (2) FlushUnconfirmed and the estimator's behaviour across a reorg (Core's processBlock height guard is present; the removeTx-on-reorg path was not driven). Inherits: dimension 9 (validation/chain reorg seam). (3) %feerate-from-value, the sat/vB decimals=3 amount parser, and the whole SetFeeEstimateMode / InterpretFeeEstimationInstructions option block - read but not probed, and they live in the wallet. Inherits: dimension 5 (wallet RPCs). (4) HexToPubKey's three distinct messages and AddAndGetMultisigDestination beyond createmultisig, which Core's tests exercise through fundrawtransaction solving_data. Inherits: dimension 5 (wallet RPCs). (5) InferDescriptor itself - the content of the desc strings we do emit was not compared against Core's inference. Inherits: dimension 1 (descriptors + signing). (6) The named-argument transform beyond what GA10 already fixed, and rpc_help.py's help-text contract, were not exercised. (7) GBTStatus / ComputeBlockVersion and the -vbparams plumbing were read only in passing; the getblocktemplate side of versionbits is a mining concern. Inherits: a mining reader. Probe caveat, recorded as lesson sbcl-coerce-derives-wrong-vector-length: (coerce X '(vector (unsigned-byte 8))) inside a local function called with vectors of several statically-known lengths returns an array of the FIRST call site's length, zero-padded, with no error - (flet ((f (x) (length (coerce x '(vector (unsigned-byte 8)))))) (list (f 22-byte) (f 1-byte) (f 3-byte))) gives (22 22 22) on SBCL 2.6.5, while putting the short vector first gives (1 3 22); a type declaration and a (vector (unsigned-byte 8) *) result type do not help. It made one ASM probe read as though every script were 22 bytes long; every ASM result above was re-run with make-array :element-type '(unsigned-byte 8) :initial-contents before being reported. The four production uses of the form (src/zmq.lisp:182, src/crypto/address.lisp:340, src/rpc/output-script.lisp:30, src/validation/script.lisp:207) were checked by execution and are correct.
